title: Granville Liggins: 1967 Sooner Nose Guard and Heisman Top 10
question: Which Oklahoma nose guard finished seventh in the 1967 Heisman Trophy voting?
answer: Granville Liggins, a Tulsa native who played for Oklahoma from 1964 to 1967, finished seventh in the 1967 Heisman voting as a nose guard. He was a consensus All-American and UPI lineman of the year that season.
summary: Granville Liggins starred at nose guard for Oklahoma, finishing seventh in the 1967 Heisman vote and becoming the first Sooner All-American in two sports.
body: Granville Liggins, a nose guard from Tulsa, played for Oklahoma from 1964 through 1967 and became one of the most decorated defensive linemen in school history. Fans often called him "Granny."

His big year was 1967. Liggins was a consensus All-American in football, and he had also been honored as an All-American in 1966. The United Press International named him its lineman of the year, and he was named Big Eight player of the year, according to his biography.

The Heisman Trophy almost never goes to a defensive lineman, but Liggins still made the ballot count. Heisman.com's list of defensive linemen in the voting shows him finishing seventh in 1967 as a nose guard for Oklahoma, the year O.J. Simpson of USC took the trophy.

Liggins was also a wrestler. He earned NCAA Division I All-America honors on the mat in 1967, which made him the first Sooner named an All-American in two sports, a distinction Bleacher Report's profile highlights.
His college finale came in the January 1968 Orange Bowl, where Oklahoma upset second-ranked Tennessee 26-24 under coach Chuck Fairbanks.

The Detroit Lions drafted him in the tenth round in 1968, but Liggins chose the Canadian Football League instead. He spent roughly a decade there, mainly with the Calgary Stampeders and Toronto Argonauts, and he was on the Calgary team that won the 1971 Grey Cup. He later made his home in Canada.
